handlingPolicy.artifactUse: Public npm tarballs were downloaded for local compatibility research, verified against npm SHA-512 integrity and a locally computed SHA-256, and never executed on the host.
handlingPolicy.fixtures: Runnable fixtures are local copies of exact tarball contents. They are gitignored and are not authorized for redistribution without package-by-package license review.
handlingPolicy.containment: Executed canaries only read static package files inside the exact digest-pinned, network-disabled Upgrade Guard container.
handlingPolicy.claimBoundary: A CHANGED receipt proves the configured static contract changed. It does not by itself reproduce a release-note claim or prove the candidate is defective.

pairs.documentedChange: 0.118.0 protected first-time project-local .codex creation; an official-repository issue reports that the same update made ordinary Linux sandboxed commands fail with bwrap permission errors.

materialRegression.impact: basic sandboxed commands can fail before execution and trigger repeated escalation prompts

pairs.canaryIdea: Resolve the platform package named by optionalDependencies, then run a Linux fixture with a project-local .codex path and assert a read-only command starts without an approval escalation.
pairs.expectedSignal: CHANGED for the wrapper dependency contract; a future platform-bundle adapter should reproduce PASS to FAIL for the sandbox-start canary.

adapter.limitation: The npm wrapper ran, but the platform binary that owns the reported behavior is a separate optional dependency and was not executed.

pairs.safetyAndLegality: Static wrapper comparison only; no Codex binary execution, account access, or credentials. Apache-2.0 registry license recorded; fixture remains local.

pairs.documentedChange: Anthropic states that 2.1.96 fixed Bedrock 403 failures involving AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK or CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH, explicitly identifying the defect as a regression in 2.1.94.

materialRegression.impact: Bedrock requests fail authorization for affected configurations
materialRegression.reproductionMethod: hash-locked published-artifact request-shape semantics with inert inputs
materialRegression.boundary: The exact deterministic pre-dispatch removal of Authorization was reproduced; no live AWS request or remote 403 response was replayed.

pairs.canaryIdea: Hash-lock the bundle, extract the Bedrock option builder and embedded SDK pre-dispatch hook as inert text, and compare AWS bearer-token plus custom-Authorization scenarios.
pairs.expectedSignal: Reproduced: 2.1.94 selects skipAuth and the embedded hook removes Authorization; 2.1.96 supplies apiKey and preserves the Bearer request shape for both vendor-named environment modes.

adapter.limitation: The generic directory adapter still refuses cli.js at 13,308,322 and 13,308,470 bytes; the purpose-built read-only tar scanner is a separate proof path.

pairs.safetyAndLegality: Tarballs were hash-locked and parsed as inert gzip/tar bytes; bundled text was not imported or executed. Registry license text requires package-specific review before redistribution; no Bedrock request, account, or credential was used.

pairs.documentedChange: The maintainer calls 3.4.0 a rollback to stable 3.2.0 because 3.3.0 concurrency changes caused some servers to hang and existing tests missed the setup-dependent failure.

materialRegression.impact: some MCP servers hang under the 3.3.0 concurrency implementation
materialRegression.reproductionMethod: hash-locked published-runtime semantics plus trusted deterministic scheduler
materialRegression.boundary: The exact default-one queued-before-transport-without-timeout causal state was reproduced; 3.4 was shown to remove that pool barrier, not proven end to end. The gateway, child server, sockets, and MCP client were not executed.

pairs.canaryIdea: Hash-lock the published runtime, extract its default capacity, acquire-before-transport, release-on-close, and unbounded-queue semantics, then schedule an idle preflight followed by a real connection.
pairs.expectedSignal: Reproduced: 3.3.0 leaves the second long-lived connection queued before transport construction without timeout behind the default-one lease; 3.4.0 has no per-session acquire barrier and both modeled requests reach the transport path.

adapter.limitation: The generic receipt observes rollback structure; the separate hash-locked scheduler proof reproduces the published causal hang state without launching vendor code.

pairs.safetyAndLegality: Published runtime files were parsed as inert text only. Registry metadata did not declare a license, so the bundled LICENSE must be reviewed before redistribution; no package code, child process, server, socket, browser, or MCP client ran.
